subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline buttons use the existing typed MessagePresentation action contract with an authenticated chat.callback Gateway RPC, and should webhook/config capability routing be in v1 or deferred?
rationale: The first implementation defines public Gateway protocol, Control UI behavior, callback security semantics, and possible config surface, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Typed presentation plus chat.callback
options.body: Use final-only MessagePresentation blocks, typed command/callback actions, and an operator-scoped Gateway RPC for clicks; defer webhook routing to a later hardened design.

options.title: Split protocol and UI phases
options.body: Land a protocol/RPC contract first and follow with Control UI rendering after real behavior proof confirms the event and callback shape.

options.title: Defer WebChat buttons
options.body: Keep current text fallback behavior until broader WebChat interaction APIs, reactions, and approval cards are designed together.

recommendation.title: Typed presentation plus chat.callback
recommendation.body: Use final-only MessagePresentation blocks, typed command/callback actions, and an operator-scoped Gateway RPC for clicks; defer webhook routing to a later hardened design.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is the shared presentation and Gateway contract shape, and this history most strongly maps to steipete's prior presentation/gateway work.
